new_statements.citation: Emeneau, M. B. 1939. The vowels of the Badaga language. Language 15(1): 43-47 (p. 44, footnote 5).
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (5 pp., text layer present; the PDF's metadata/extracted text) and rendered page 2 (= Language 15: 44) to PNG. Footnote 5 reads exactly "All words of more than one syllable are accented on the first syllable." It is attached to the sentence closing the vowel-phoneme list in the phonology section ("..all the 29 phonemes which occur are distinct entities.5"); no other prosodic remark in the article. Reading fixed: initial syllable is right: the statement is categorical, word-level ("All words of more than one syllable"), no weight/morphology conditions, no secondary stress, no exceptions; "accented" is the 1930s term for stress. Status statement found in an open source is right: the sa…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent is fixed on the first syllable of every polysyllabic word; no conditions of weight or morphology are stated.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the footnote is categorical ('All words').
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement made in a phonological description of the Kateri (Ketti-area) dialect from Emeneau's 1937-8 fieldwork; single footnote, no phonetic detail. Hockings 1980: 40 n. 1 independently says the name 'Badaga' is pronounced with stress on the first syllable. The 2023 Registrar General LSI Tamil Nadu chapter treats only length and nasalisation as suprasegmentals and is silent on stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Emeneau 1939 explicitly describes only the dialect 'spoken in the neighborhood of Kateri' (Ketti area, Nilgiris), noting that speakers report other dialects on which no work had been done; this is Badaga proper (bada1257), not a differently named variety. The 2023 LSI chapter and Hockings's works treat the general Nilgiri Badaga community language.
